tool_input.description: Run scratch program to inspect actual quote/escape and integer formatting behavior

result:
Done. Created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/text/ExtendedMessageFormatAgentTest.java` with 23 self-contained JUnit 3.8-style (`junit.framework.TestCase`) test methods covering:

- Construction with/without locale/registry, equivalence to plain `MessageFormat`
- Custom `FormatFactory` registry usage (with/without format arguments), fallback to built-in formats when the registry doesn't match
- `toPattern()` round-tripping with custom and mixed format elements
- Quoting/escaping behavior (`''`, quoted literal braces)
- Boundary/error cases: unterminated format element, invalid argument index, unterminated quote inside a format description, empty pattern, pattern with no format elements
- The disabled mutators (`setFormat`, `setFormatByArgumentIndex`, `setFormats`, `setFormatsByArgumentIndex`) throwing `UnsupportedOperationException`
- `equals()`/`hashCode()` contract including null, different type, different pattern, and different registry cases

All assertions check returned/observable values (formatted strings, patterns, factory call arguments), not just absence of exceptions. The investigation used temporary scratch files outside `src/` to probe actual runtime behavior (since this class has some quirky quote-handling edge cases), which were removed afterward — only the test file itself was added. `./_tools/test.sh` passes with all 23 tests green.
